cases.scenario: An active worker owns implementation and tests while Sol prepares an explicitly separate release note.
cases.expected_outcome: Allow explicitly allowed orthogonal primary prep; the active worker keeps implementation and test ownership.

cases.scenario: An explorer is active on the caller trace and Sol starts the same evidence search.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny same-scope primary explorer duplication; wait for or correct the existing explorer instead.

cases.scenario: A worker owns tracked implementation and tests while Sol attempts to edit and run those tests.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny primary edits and same-scope tests while worker is active; worker owns tracked tests/config/dependencies.

cases.scenario: A tester owns the browser session while Sol attempts a second browser QA session.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny primary browser QA while tester is active; the same tester owns browser/runtime QA end to end.

cases.scenario: A reviewer phase depends on a worker that is still active.
cases.expected_outcome: Wait for the acceptance-relevant worker to reach terminal state and inspect its handoff before dependent reviewer work.

cases.scenario: The worker is terminal but the acceptance-relevant tester remains active when Sol attempts acceptance.
cases.expected_outcome: Wait for every acceptance-relevant child, including the active tester, before accepting; unrelated terminal evidence does not waive the barrier.

cases.scenario: A failed acceptance-relevant worker has no Sol disposition and acceptance is requested.
cases.expected_outcome: Record and resolve failed-child disposition before treating it as terminal; missing evidence cannot be silently waived.

cases.scenario: A blocked acceptance-relevant tester has no Sol disposition and dependent validation is requested.
cases.expected_outcome: Record and resolve blocked tester disposition before dependent validation; do not accept partial or missing browser evidence.

cases.scenario: An active child is quiet and stale, but no safety or evidence-supported abandonment exists.
cases.expected_outcome: Silence and elapsed time alone are not abandonment; prefer a long wait_agent and do not interrupt or duplicate the child.

cases.scenario: wait_agent yields only a timeout with no new child output, blocker, state transition, or user decision.
cases.expected_outcome: Keep the internal wait silent: emit no user-facing status/chatter without new output, blocker, state transition, or needed user decision.

cases.scenario: wait_agent returns new child evidence.
cases.expected_outcome: A new child return is a factual update permitted after a quiet wait.

cases.scenario: A child transitions state while Sol waits.
cases.expected_outcome: An actual child state transition permits a concise user-facing update.

cases.scenario: A child reports an explicit blocker while Sol waits.
cases.expected_outcome: An explicit blocker permits a concise factual update and a return to Sol for disposition.

cases.scenario: A user decision arrives while Sol waits.
cases.expected_outcome: A needed user decision permits a concise user-facing update after waiting.

cases.scenario: A second native role attempts evidence work inside an active worker's owned scope.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny cross-role overlap; the active child's scope lock applies to primary and other native child actors.

cases.scenario: A bounded explorer question is disjoint from an active worker's owned files.
cases.expected_outcome: Allow explicitly non-overlapping cross-role evidence scope while preserving one-writer ownership.

cases.scenario: A tester writer starts a disjoint write while an active worker already owns the shared worktree.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny a second writer even on a disjoint scope; shared-worktree one-writer ownership is global.

cases.scenario: The worker succeeded and Sol inspected its handoff and artifacts before review.
cases.expected_outcome: After terminal handoff and artifact inspection, allow the dependent reviewer phase.

cases.scenario: The worker reports success but Sol has not inspected a required artifact before dependent validation.
cases.expected_outcome: Wait for handoff and artifact inspection; successful status alone cannot waive required evidence.

cases.scenario: Every acceptance-relevant child succeeded and Sol inspected each handoff and artifact before ACCEPT.
cases.expected_outcome: Allow ACCEPT only after all acceptance-relevant predecessors are terminal and their handoffs and artifacts are inspected.

cases.scenario: An authorized interruption is terminal only after Sol records its disposition; ACCEPT arrives before that record.
cases.expected_outcome: Wait for disposition of an interrupted predecessor; an authorized interruption does not silently waive required evidence.

cases.scenario: An active explorer owns a bounded reconnaissance trace while Sol attempts the same recon.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny primary recon inside an active explorer's owned evidence scope.

cases.scenario: A deep explorer owns an architecture-sensitive trace while Sol attempts the same recon.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny primary recon inside an active deep_explorer's architecture-sensitive evidence scope.

cases.scenario: A reviewer owns a review scope while Sol attempts to take over that review.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny primary review takeover while the assigned reviewer is active.

cases.scenario: Sol has explicit evidence-supported abandonment and interrupts the active child.
cases.expected_outcome: Allow interrupt only for user stop, safety boundary, or evidence-supported abandonment.

cases.scenario: Sol wants to interrupt because a child is quiet, without user stop, safety, or abandonment evidence.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny elapsed-time-only interruption; silence is not abandonment.

cases.scenario: A cited explorer handoff is fresh across all reuse dimensions.
cases.expected_outcome: Reuse cited evidence because scope, branch/base, dirty ownership, relevant config/runtime, contracts, and path are unchanged.

cases.scenario: A cited explorer handoff is followed by branch/base, ownership, runtime, and contract drift.
cases.expected_outcome: Invalidate and recon or correct the same child when scope, branch/base, ownership, config/runtime, contracts, contradiction, or path changes.

cases.scenario: The cited evidence does not establish the needed runtime path.
cases.expected_outcome: Do not reuse evidence while the needed path remains unknown; invalidate and run bounded RECON.

cases.scenario: A failed acceptance-relevant worker has a structured Sol disposition, but its missing outcome still cannot be accepted.
cases.expected_outcome: A disposition is inspectable control evidence but does not silently waive an acceptance-relevant failed predecessor.

cases.scenario: A successful worker has an inspected handoff and artifact but has not completed declared evidence.
cases.expected_outcome: Wait for explicit evidence_complete and all declared required_evidence before acceptance.

cases.scenario: Every acceptance-relevant predecessor is terminal, inspected, and complete with its declared evidence.
cases.expected_outcome: Allow acceptance only when every relevant predecessor's handoff, artifacts, and declared evidence are inspected and complete.

cases.scenario: Sol explicitly rescopes a failed child out of acceptance after inspecting its structured disposition and artifacts.
cases.expected_outcome: A non-relevant rescope is allowed only with inspectable structured disposition and complete handoff evidence.

cases.scenario: Sol's preparation includes one allowed documentation item and one undeclared implementation item.
cases.expected_outcome: Directional coverage rejects an orthogonal request containing any undeclared scope item.

cases.scenario: A cited evidence snapshot covers one API contract but the requested reuse adds an unproven extra scope item.
cases.expected_outcome: Evidence reuse requires the cited snapshot scope to directionally cover every requested scope item.

cases.scenario: A matching evidence snapshot has no inspectable handoff identifier.
cases.expected_outcome: Do not reuse a snapshot without explicit nonempty inspectable provenance.

cases.scenario: The assigned worker continues its own active write within its fully covered scope.
cases.expected_outcome: The assigned child may continue its own owned action; its own record is excluded from overlap and writer self-conflict checks.

cases.scenario: A worker child attempts work inside another active worker child's assignment.
cases.expected_outcome: A different child cannot overlap an active child's assignment even when it has a valid native role.

cases.scenario: A read-only tester is active while Sol prepares an explicitly disjoint documentation note.
cases.expected_outcome: A read-only tester does not falsely become a shared-worktree writer and does not block disjoint authorized preparation.

cases.scenario: A tester explicitly authorized to repair files attempts a disjoint write while the worker owns the shared worktree.
cases.expected_outcome: Explicit tester writer ownership collides with another writer globally, even on disjoint files.

cases.scenario: A worker proposes a write outside the scope assigned to its child identity.
cases.expected_outcome: A child identity must directionally cover its requested scope; an unrelated file is an escape.

cases.scenario: A reviewer supplies valid-looking state but attempts to control ACCEPT.
cases.expected_outcome: Only Sol primary may authorize ACCEPT; a reviewer cannot take over primary control.

cases.scenario: A tester has a valid user-stop reason but attempts to interrupt another child.
cases.expected_outcome: Only Sol primary may interrupt children; a valid reason does not grant a child control authority.

cases.scenario: An explorer is active while Sol proposes a disjoint write that is absent from the primary ownership ledger.
cases.expected_outcome: Deny every substantive primary action not fully covered by an explicit orthogonal ledger entry while a child is active.

cases.scenario: An assigned reviewer attempts to edit the review file in its own review scope.
cases.expected_outcome: Reviewer identity does not authorize product writes; reviewers may perform review actions only.

cases.scenario: An assigned explorer attempts a write inside its own evidence scope.
cases.expected_outcome: Explorer identity authorizes evidence and recon only, never implementation writes.

cases.scenario: An assigned explorer presents a complete evidence snapshot but attempts Sol-primary evidence reuse control.
cases.expected_outcome: Evidence reuse is a Sol-primary decision even when an explorer owns and can cite the underlying handoff.

cases.scenario: A relevant worker is complete while an unrelated non-relevant failed explorer has no rescope request.
cases.expected_outcome: Ignore a completely unrelated failed child; only relevant predecessors and explicit rescope children enter the acceptance barrier.

cases.scenario: A tester has writer ownership but no explicit repair authorization metadata for a product write.
cases.expected_outcome: Action-supplied repair flags cannot authorize a tester; the Sol-owned child ledger must contain the repair authorization.

cases.scenario: Sol records a narrow failed-check repair authorization on the assigned tester ledger.
cases.expected_outcome: Allow only the exact Sol-ledger-authorized product repair after matching the authorization round.

cases.scenario: A tester with repair metadata attempts the generic write action.
cases.expected_outcome: Generic tester writes remain forbidden even when a Sol repair ledger entry exists.

cases.scenario: A tester attempts the generic edit action rather than the narrow repair action.
cases.expected_outcome: Tester may not turn a repair authorization into a generic edit.

cases.scenario: A tester attempts tracked configuration work owned by the worker.
cases.expected_outcome: Tracked configuration and dependency/setup changes remain worker-owned.

cases.scenario: A tester attempts the worker-owned combined edit and test action.
cases.expected_outcome: A tester repair is never a generic worker edit-and-test phase.

cases.scenario: A tester repair authorization has no failed-check identifier.
cases.expected_outcome: A product repair must point to a specific failed check recorded by Sol.

cases.scenario: A tester repair requests a path outside the Sol-ledger authorization scope.
cases.expected_outcome: Repair paths are directionally covered by the Sol-owned authorization, not caller-selected.

cases.scenario: A tester repair uses a different correction round from the Sol ledger.
cases.expected_outcome: A repair action must use the exact correction/authorization round in the child ledger.

cases.scenario: A valid tester repair writer attempts a disjoint write while the worker is active.
cases.expected_outcome: Even a narrow authorized tester repair cannot create a second shared-worktree writer.

cases.scenario: Sol cites an inspected succeeded explorer handoff with a matching evidence digest and snapshot.
cases.expected_outcome: Reuse is allowed only after provenance resolves to the inspected handoff ledger entry.

cases.scenario: A snapshot cites a handoff identifier absent from the state ledger.
cases.expected_outcome: An unknown handoff cannot establish evidence provenance.

cases.scenario: A handoff exists but provenance names a different child identity.
cases.expected_outcome: Provenance must resolve to the exact child that produced the inspected handoff.

cases.scenario: A succeeded explorer handoff exists but Sol has not inspected it.
cases.expected_outcome: A handoff is not reusable until its ledger inspection flag is true.

cases.scenario: The cited explorer handoff belongs to a failed child.
cases.expected_outcome: Failed child output cannot be cited as fresh reusable evidence.

cases.scenario: The cited handoff digest does not match the provenance digest.
cases.expected_outcome: A handoff digest mismatch invalidates provenance instead of trusting caller-supplied evidence.

cases.scenario: The cited handoff snapshot differs from the requested evidence snapshot.
cases.expected_outcome: Every reuse dimension must match the inspected handoff snapshot before current-state freshness is considered.

cases.scenario: The requested reuse scope adds a path outside the inspected handoff scope.
cases.expected_outcome: A fully covered handoff scope is required; an extra requested path invalidates reuse.

cases.scenario: State attempts to expand evidence reuse to a worker handoff.
cases.expected_outcome: A state-supplied allowed_evidence_roles list cannot admit worker evidence; reuse is fixed to explorer roles.

cases.scenario: State attempts to expand evidence reuse to a tester handoff.
cases.expected_outcome: A state-supplied allowed_evidence_roles list cannot admit tester evidence; reuse is fixed to explorer roles.

cases.scenario: State attempts to expand evidence reuse to a reviewer handoff.
cases.expected_outcome: A state-supplied allowed_evidence_roles list cannot admit reviewer evidence; reuse is fixed to explorer roles.

cases.scenario: The inspected handoff claims a broader scope than its cited explorer child owns.
cases.expected_outcome: Handoff scope must be directionally covered by the cited child ledger before reuse can proceed.

cases.scenario: Current evidence contains an empty branch value instead of a known freshness dimension.
cases.expected_outcome: An empty current evidence freshness dimension is malformed and cannot be reused.

cases.scenario: The requested evidence snapshot contains an empty contracts list.
cases.expected_outcome: An empty snapshot freshness dimension is malformed and cannot be reused.

cases.scenario: The inspected handoff contains an object in the base freshness dimension.
cases.expected_outcome: A malformed handoff freshness dimension invalidates provenance before reuse.
